title: Biology - Core Terms and Basic Structures

cards.front: Name six commonly used characteristics of living things.
cards.back: Cellular organization, metabolism, growth and development, response to stimuli, reproduction, and heredity with adaptation.

cards.front: Order the levels of organization from small to large.
cards.back: Cell - tissue - organ - organ system - organism.

cards.front: Name central components of a plant cell.
cards.back: Cell wall, cell membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, chloroplasts, vacuole, and mitochondria.

cards.front: What is the basic function of the plant cell wall?
cards.back: It gives the cell shape, stability, and protection.

cards.front: What is the basic function of chloroplasts?
cards.back: Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts; light energy is used there to build energy-rich substances.

cards.front: What is the basic function of the nucleus?
cards.back: The nucleus contains genetic information and controls many cell processes.

cards.front: What does the RGT rule state for enzymatic reactions?
cards.back: A temperature increase of 10 °C often raises the reaction rate to about two to three times the previous value, as long as no temperature maximum or denaturation has been reached.

cards.front: Name four basic parts of a flower.
cards.back: Sepals, petals, stamens, and carpel or pistil.

cards.front: What is the function of stamens?
What is the function of the carpel or pistil?
cards.back: It contains the ovules and receives pollen through the stigma.

cards.front: Name the main components of blood.
cards.back: Blood plasma, red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets.

cards.front: What is the main task of red blood cells?
What is the main task of white blood cells?
cards.back: They are part of the immune defense.

cards.front: What is the main task of platelets?
cards.back: They are important for blood clotting.
A karyogram shows the chromosomes of a cell arranged by size, shape, and pairs.

cards.front: How many chromosomes does a normal human body cell have?

cards.back: Chromosome 21 is present three times instead of twice.
